Use a Tier 2 change focused on model_design and training_evaluation: replace uniformly sampled training negatives with model-driven hard-negative sampling while preserving the existing network. The latest model reaches macro validation HR@10 of 0.5037, with Electronics at 0.38 versus the baseline’s 0.42, so the added history mechanism has not established an overall improvement. One plausible limitation is that 256 uniformly sampled negatives provide too few competitive alternatives once the model learns to reject easy items.

For each selected training transition, sample a pool of 1,024 candidate negatives and score them using the current network’s sequence features, item embeddings, and learned item biases. Exclude all items in that user’s complete training history and the transition’s positive target, then construct the sampled-softmax denominator from the 64 highest-scoring eligible negatives and 192 randomly selected remaining negatives. Detach scores during negative selection, but compute the resulting ranking loss through the selected items and sequence features normally. This single change concentrates learning on ranking mistakes while retaining random negatives for coverage; keep the architecture, transition weighting, optimizer, and other training settings unchanged for a controlled comparison.

Train one independent model per category with training seed 42, consume the existing splits unchanged, and retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Select exactly one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 on the fixed 200 users and 99 unique negatives with evaluation seed 42, reporting the four-category macro average without accessing hidden test data. Keep dataset routing and the predictor writer aligned with the saved architecture so every host prediction comes directly from its category’s single trained checkpoint.
